claim: From 18 February 2027 each LMT battery, EV battery and industrial battery above 2 kWh placed on the market or put into service requires a battery passport with model and individual-battery data.

From 18 February 2027 covered batteries require a QR code leading to the passport; marking must be visible, legible and indelible on the battery or, where appropriate, packaging/documents. The QR links to a placing-operator-assigned unique identifier and both must comply with the listed ISO/IEC 15459 family or equivalent.

For reused, repurposed or remanufactured batteries, passport responsibility transfers to the new placing operator and a new passport must link to the original passport(s); new status markings are also required.

The placing operator remains responsible for accurate, complete and current passport data even when another operator is authorised, and passport information must use open, interoperable, machine-readable formats without vendor lock-in.
Article 78 requires role-based access, continued availability, authentication, integrity, security/privacy and restricted processor reuse.

Since 18 August 2024 stationary BESS, LMT and EV batteries must contain current health/lifetime parameters in the BMS, with read-only purchaser/authorised-party access for specified purposes including valuation and repurposing.
The EU DPP Registry went live on 20 July 2026 with a testing environment; it stores identifiers/metadata while full passport data remain decentralised with the operator or provider.
The Commission's August 2026 battery guidance organises 71 data points by category and expressly says the guidance is non-authoritative and creates no new requirements.
On 1 September 2026 the Commission timeline scheduled two remaining DPP standards for September 2026, battery access-rights rules for Q4 2026 and service-provider delegated requirements for 2027.
ESPR uses product-specific delegated acts for concrete DPP requirements; the Commission says operators receive at least an 18-month transition after such an act.

claim: The Commission's 2025-2030 working plan prioritises steel, aluminium, textiles/apparel, furniture, tyres and mattresses among other measures/products.
Battery due diligence begins 18 August 2027 after the 2025 amendment; Chapter VII has a EUR 40m turnover threshold and excludes previously marketed batteries later reused/repurposed/remanufactured.
Siemens offers a Battery Passport REST API with user and passport create/read/update/delete operations.
Circularise markets model- and individual-battery data, QR access and user permissions in one battery-passport platform.
Minespider markets EU battery-passport tooling and an open API.
